ruling.recommended_action: Escalate to a Ryde reviewer: determine which road the 12:29–12:39 segment was actually driven on and whether the rider's 12:27 "Sure, go ahead." (F9) to the driver's named-road proposal (F8) covers it; if it does not, refund 3.27 km × $1.4098/km = $4.61 (RD-2). No account flag (RD-6 not met).
ruling.reasoning:
The trip is a metered RydeTAXI ride: the fare record decomposes into distance $27.35 over 19.40 km plus time and waiting components [F7][F4], so any refund falls on the mileage branch of RD-2, not the fixed-quote branch. The rider's own brief concedes this [C3][D1]. The GPS record shows one off-route segment, 12:29–12:39, 6.34 km driven where the optimal route covers 3.07 km, i.e. 3.27 km extra [F3][RD-1].

The exemption turns on RD-5. The driver proposed "ok if I go round via Sims Avenue?" at 12:26 [F8], and the rider's own message "Sure, go ahead." at 12:27 [F9] precedes the segment start of 12:29 — so this is genuine rider consent sent before the segment began, and the driver's post-trip statement [F11] is not needed to establish it (and could not establish it alone, G11). The dispute is therefore about the SCOPE of that consent, not its existence [RD-5].

The wording is a SPECIFIC named-road authorisation: the proposal names one road, Sims Avenue [F8], and the rider's "Sure, go ahead." adopts exactly that proposal [F9]. Under RD-5, a named-road agreement covers driving on that road only, and the record must tie the driven segment to that road; timing alone does not, and the fact table carries no road names for the driven path [F3][F10]. Nothing ties the segment to Sims Avenue, and nothing places it elsewhere: the driver's statement [F11] repeats only "turning off via Sims Avenue" and names no other road, and F3 records no stop or road name. That is the G13 situation — undetermined [F3][F10][F8][F9][RD-5]. I do not read "ok if I go round via Sims Avenue?" as a general route licence: it is a proposal on a named road, not "whichever way is faster" [F8][RD-5].

The RD-4 branch gives the driver nothing: no traffic incident is recorded near the route in the trip window [F14], so RD-4(a) fails; the only congestion item is a PIE speed band 2 record [F12], and RD-4(b) says a band record alone does not exempt a segment. The driver's own statement about traffic [F11] is a statement, not a traffic fact, and RD-4 requires a traffic fact [F11][F12][F14][RD-4]. That part of the case is settled against the driver, but it is not what decides the amount.

The amount: if the segment counts, RD-2 gives the unexempted segment's extra_km times this trip's per-km rate, being fare.distance_fare ÷ distance_km = $27.35 ÷ 19.40 km = $1.4098/km, so 3.27 km × $1.4098/km = $4.61 [F3][F4][F7][RD-2]. The billed excess-distance line of $5.54 is 3.93 km × $1.4098/km and includes ~0.66 km of corridor/matching mileage not attributable to any segment, which RD-2 does not refund; both advocates concede this [F4][F1][C3][D2]. The $0.11 metered waiting charge is payable on a RydeTAXI meter and is not contested [F5][F7][RD-3].

Because the scope of the rider's consent is the element that fixes whether the amount is $4.61 or $0.00, and the record cannot settle it, the case must go to a person rather than be decided on an undetermined finding [RD-5][G13]. No account flag applies: the trace and the profile show route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 [F17], so RD-6's repeated-breach precondition is not met [RD-6].

Safety screen: I read the complaint, both chat messages [F8][F9] and the driver's statement [F11]. They contain a route/traffic discussion and an agreement to it only — no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation [SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. Safety_concern = none.

Evidence: the chat is complete and fully timestamped [F10], and the GPS and fare records are present [F3][F4][F7], so the case does not fail on missing records (no GPS hole, no untimed message). The gap is not a missing record but an absent link between the agreed named road and the driven path — a question the materials do not settle, which per G13 goes to a human.

segment_findings.reason: The driver proposed a specific named road ('ok if I go round via Sims Avenue?', 12:26 [F8]) and the rider's own message agreed before the segment start ('Sure, go ahead.', 12:27 < 12:29 [F9][F3]), so consent exists; but a named-road agreement under RD-5 covers driving on that road only and the record must tie the segment to it. Nothing does: the fact table carries no road names for the driven path [F3][F10], there is no stop or message placing the car on Sims Avenue, and the driver's statement [F11] names no other road either. Timing alone cannot tie them (G13), so the scope of the consent is undetermined. This drives the amount ($4.61 if it counts, $0.00 if exempt), so the case goes to a human [RD-5].

rejected_claims.reason: Accepted as to the raw distances [F1][F2], but the +3.9 km / +25% total does not itself establish a refundable breach: RD-1 is applied segment by segment [F3][RD-1], and only 3.27 km is attributable to the single off-route segment [F3].

Rejected as to quantum: RD-2 refunds Σ(unexempted segment extra_km) × this trip's per-km rate, i.e. 3.27 km × $1.4098/km = $4.61 [F3][F4][F7][RD-2]; the billed line of $5.54 (3.93 km) includes ~0.66 km of corridor/matching mileage outside any segment, which RD-2 expressly does not refund.

Accepted on RD-4 but not decisive here: no qualifying incident [F14] and a speed band alone does not exempt [F12][RD-4]; that removes the driver's reasonable-cause defence without settling the RD-5 scope question, which is what fixes the amount [F3][F8][F9][RD-5].
Accepted — this is a RydeTAXI metered fare [F7] and any refund is mileage-only under RD-2 [F4][F7][RD-2]; the rider's revised ask already conforms [C3].

Accepted as to scope (the residual ~0.66 km is not refundable under RD-2 [F1][F3][F4][RD-2]), but rejected as to outcome: it assumes the segment is exempt, which the record does not settle [F3][F8][F9][F10][RD-5].

Accepted that rider consent exists before the segment [F8][F9][F3][RD-5]; it does not follow that the 6.34 km segment is covered, because the agreement named a road the record does not tie to the driven path [F3][F10][RD-5].

Rejected: RD-4 requires a traffic fact and a speed band alone does not exempt [F12][F14][RD-4]; the driver's post-trip assertion of traffic build-up [F11] is a statement, and SAFE-1/RD-4 do not convert it into evidence.

Accepted: route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 [F17], so RD-6's precondition is unmet and no flag_account arises; the same reasoning is why the amount here turns only on the RD-5 scope, not on repetition [RD-6].
